Counting and Grouping

CountingArithmeticDivisibility
Game: A heap of dots is waiting to be counted; there is nothing to win or lose.
How to play: Press the dots one by one to count them. A tally of strokes grows underneath in groups, and when you finish it becomes a sum.

Look for the math

Counting is putting the dots in a row and giving each one the next number. Grouping is a way of doing the same work in bigger steps.

Groups and what is left over

Counting 14 strokes in groups of 3 gives four full groups and 2 left over: 14 = 4 × 3 + 2. In general, every whole number N and group size g have a unique q and r with N = q·g + r and 0 ≤ r < g: this is division with remainder. The logic test checked the tally and both equations for every N up to 200 and every group size up to 220.

The remainder is the residue

The leftover r is the residue of N modulo g. Change the group size and watch it change while the number of dots stays put: with 12 dots, groups of 5 leave 2, groups of 4 leave nothing. The applet's own title is “Dot patterns & modular arithmetic”.

Two ways to say it

The equation is shown as a repeated sum, 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 2 = 14, and as a product, 4 × 3 + 2 = 14: multiplication is repeated addition. The applet leaves out the long sum when there is at most one full group, and for groups of 1 once there are 20 dots or more.

Choose 12 dots and try every group size from 1 to 13. For which sizes is nothing left over?
